correctness.rationale: On the zero-sum vertex space, the Laplacian is N I−ddᵀ for d=e₀−e₁. Its inverse there is I/N+ddᵀ/[N(N−2)] since dᵀd=2. For an incident edge 0x the potential has values (N−1)/[N(N−2)], −1/[N(N−2)], −1/N at 0,1,x respectively, and zero elsewhere. Summing the absolute differences along surviving edges gives q_A=2−1/(N−2) with diagonal r_A=(2N−3)/[N(N−2)]. For a remote edge, the rank-one term vanishes and the omitted edge would have had zero drop; q_B=2−2/N and r_B=2/N. Since 0≤r_e≤1 for an orthogonal projector, complementary absolute column sums are 1+q_e−2r_e. The two orbit differences are therefore (N−4)/[N(N−2)] and (N−6)/[N(N−2)]. Both orbits exist only for N≥4; their maxima give the signs and ties stated. For N=3 the surviving graph is a tree with Q=I and P=0. For the full clique, every cut column has diagonal 2/N and 2(N−2) entries of magnitude 1/N, so the full clique values are 2−2/N and 3−6/N. Symmetry of the projections identifies the two endpoint norms, and orientation only changes row and column signs.
